newsitem.title: USA: US Treasuries trade higher on core PPI.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries trade higher on core PPI.

text.p: U.S. Treasury prices traded higher on Thursday after the government said wholesale prices, excluding food and energy, edged lower in August.
Economists and market participants had expected those prices to rise slightly.
The overall Producer Price Index (PPI) did rise 0.3 percent, mostly due to higher energy and food prices.
But the inflation-conscious bond market pays more attention to the so-called core PPI, the index minus its more volatile food and energy items. That core slipped 0.1 percent.
At midday, the benchmark 30 year bond was trading at 96-3/32, up 18/32, to yield 7.06 percent.
Analysts said the inflation data has some traders betting the Federal Reserve will not raise interest rates by more than 25 basis points at the September 24 meeting.

"The market pushed higher on core PPI," said Steve Ricchuito, chief financial economist at Barclays de Zoete Woeld Government Securities. "It was lower than people thought, so it diffused some of the talk of a larger than 25-basis-point (rate rise)."

The Atlanta Fed Survey of business activity for August came in at 4.0 percent versus a revised minus 1.2 percent in July. Analyts say the report had little impact on trading, but confirmed that some regions of the economy are quite strong.
"The sharp movement up could lead people to say the manufacturing sector is still doing well," Ricchuito said.
Jobless claims for the week ending September 7 rose to 338,000 from 317,000 the previous week. Market watchers say the stronger figures reinforced the gains the bond market made on the PPI numbers.

"The market was a little bit influenced by the initial claims data," Michael Moran, chief economist at Daiwa Securities said. "It wasn't necessarily a meaningful move, but it reinforced PPI and gave the market a lift."
Moran said the economic news was not enough, however, to change market sentiment about a Fed rate hike at month end.
"We need to see CPI tomorrow. If CPI shows even the slightest hint of price pressure, people will forget PPI," Moran said. "The market and Fed officials give more weight to CPI."
Moran added he expects the market to hold at current levels for the remainder of the trading day.
Analysts said the market is likely to remain cautious ahead of August's consumer price Index (CPI) and retail sales figures scheduled for release on Friday.

"If anything the PPI report raises the risk of a higher CPI because of the higher food and energy costs," said Michael Strauss, chief economist at Yamaichi International (America) Inc. "The market is anticipating (lower) than 0.2 percent and I think it's unlikely."
Strauss expects price pressures from airlines, apparel, entertainment and college tuition to show up in the August CPI.
The consensus forecast calls for a 0.2 percent rise in both the overall and core rates of the August CPI.
Retail sales figures for August are expected to rise 0.7 percent and 0.4 percent excluding autos.
At the short end of the maturity range, three-month bill rates were down two basis points to 5.14 percent and six-month bill rates were down three basis points to 5.26 percent.
The two-year notes were up 4/32 to 99-24/32, yielding 6.26 percent. Five-years rose 9/32 to 99-15/32, yielding 6.63 percent. Ten-years were up 13/32 to 100-30/32, yielding 6.87 percent.
